findings.statement: verifying block checksums costs nothing on a cold scan
findings.detail: cold scans at 39251416 entries/s verified against 54902165 unverified (verified vs unverified: less 0.715x (p=0.0022, rel_iqr 4.5%/4.6%)). f8-checksums measured this cost at no difference on point reads, where a block is checked once and read many times; a scan over a fresh reader touches each block for the first time and pays for all of them

findings.statement: a scan's first pass costs no more than its steady state
findings.detail: verified: 39251416 entries/s cold against 64728457 warm (1.65x). Unverified: 54902165 against 59719922 (1.09x). Whatever remains after the checksum is subtracted is the cost of touching the mapping for the first time, and the cold pass took 0 major faults with 0.0% of its wall time off CPU

notes: one file with checksums in it; the arms differ only in whether the reader verifies them. A fresh reader per repetition is what makes the first pass cold
